prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your home, budget, timeline and service expectations. I can help find top-rated options near you if you tell me your zip code and any priorities (price, brand, fast install, financing, etc.). Meanwhile, here’s how to find the best company and a few reputable names to consider in Atlanta.

How to pick the right contractor
- Get at least 3 written estimates for the exact same scope of work.
- Require a load calculation (Manual J) to size the system properly (not just “rule of thumb” sizing).
- Verify they are licensed, insured, and have NATE-certified technicians (or equivalent).
- Ask about brand options, SEER rating, and warranties (both manufacturer and installer).
- Confirm who pulls permits and handles disposal of the old unit.
- Check recent local reviews on Google, BBB, Angi/HomeAdvisor and ask for references from similar installs.
- Compare installed cost, expected runtime (efficiency gains), estimated completion date, and a written service/maintenance plan.
- Ask about financing, rebates, and whether they’ll inspect/repair ductwork as part of the job.

Typical costs in Atlanta (ballpark)
- Small central AC (2–3 ton): roughly $3,500–$6,000 installed.
- Medium (3–4 ton): roughly $5,000–$8,000.
- Larger homes (4–5+ ton / higher-efficiency units): $7,000–$12,000+.
Prices vary by brand, SEER rating, ductwork condition, and installation complexity.

Brands commonly recommended
- Trane, Carrier, Lennox, Rheem, Goodman. Trane/Carrier/Lennox often have higher upfront cost and strong reliability; Goodman and Rheem are often more budget-friendly. Ask about specific model warranties.

Local companies to consider (verify credentials & get quotes)
- Coolray (has strong presence in Atlanta and many positive reviews)
- One Hour Heating & Air / Benjamin Franklin franchise locations
- ARS / Rescue Rooter / Service Experts (national brands with local offices)
- Local independent contractors with high Google/BBB ratings — a well-reviewed local company can be as good or better than a national brand.

What I can do next
- If you give your zip code, house size (sq ft), number of floors, and whether you have existing ducts, I’ll pull (or suggest how to find) 3–5 highly rated contractors near you and a checklist of questions to ask when you call for quotes.
